newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia Hansapank happy with '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Estonia Hansapank happy with '96 profit.

text.p: Estonia's leading bank, Hansapank, said on Thursday that it was pleased with its 1996 results as they were higher than planned.
The bank also held out the hope that it may pay dividends, although the final decision rested with the bank's shareholders.
It said 1996 non-consolidated profit of 234.4 million kroons was higher than planned as was net asset growth of 64.2 percent.
"The market share of Hansapank increased to 25.3 percent in 1996 against 22.7 percent a year earlier, following the net asset growth," Hansapank analyst Kristina Siimar told a news conference.
The bank said it made an extraordinary profit of more than 100 million kroons after it sold its stake in second biggest Estonian bank Savings Bank.
But it invested 70 million kroons in buying the Latvian Deutsche-Lettische Bank, now called Hansabank-Latvija.
Board members said that a portion of the profit could be paid out as dividends with the rest staying undistributed.
"A one-off dividend payment is fairly possible," Tiina Mois, a board member said.
Hansapank said Hansabank-Latvija had net assets of 1.4 billion kroons in 1996 and made a loss of 1.2 million kroons.
The forecast for 1997 for Hansabank-Latvija is for a 20 million kroon profit and net assets of 1.7 billion kroons.
